$comment: Machine-readable freshness registry — the single source of truth for WHEN every data class is meant to refresh and how stale it is allowed to get. Consumed by scripts/check_freshness.mjs (CI/owner check), lib/freshness.ts (the /api/freshness route and the /api/cron/freshness-audit cron), validate-data (WARN wiring), and next.config.mjs, which derives the outputFileTracingIncludes entry for every field-stamped artifact from this file so both freshness functions are deployed with the files they open at runtime. See docs/WAYFINDER_LIVE_DATA.md for the cadence table and activation matrix. Keep entries in lockstep with vercel.json, app/api/cron, remaining workflows, and refresh scripts.

datasets.label: London pint-price dataset

stamp.consumedBy: lib/dataFreshness.ts PINT_DATASET_OBSERVED_AT (build-time import; this stamp is the single source of truth for the pint dataset's collection date — the TS constant is derived from it, never hand-authored)

datasets.cadence: episodic — re-collected by hand, then re-exported
datasets.gate: none (bundled static; keyless)

datasets.label: Cheapest-pint baseline price updates
datasets.cadence: advances only when a reviewed publish re-commits the artifact; the weekly Vercel retrieval sweep cannot write this file
datasets.refreshWorkflow: manual reviewed publish via npm run refresh:prices -- --open-pr. The weekly Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-prices only RETRIEVES rows and stamps the separate price_update_retrieval feed; it never advances this dataset, because a read-only serverless FS cannot rewrite the served file.
datasets.gate: none to run; first-party parsers are STUBBED (fetchFromSource returns []), so scheduled runs remain honest no-ops and this feed stays visibly stale until a real parser retrieves valid rows AND a human publishes them

datasets.label: Permissible-source price retrieval (scheduled sweep, unpublished)
datasets.cadence: weekly, Monday 07:00 UTC via Vercel cron
datasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-prices retrieves and validates first-party/open-data rows, then stamps feed_freshness (durable store, migration 0047 plane) only when at least one valid row was fetched; empty, invalid, or failed runs log the no-op and preserve the prior stamp. Store-only, no committed artifact: /api/freshness and the freshness-audit cron both read the store's real observedAt directly (never a disk fallback, because none exists), and scripts/check_freshness.mjs queries the same table dependency-free. A store the checker cannot reach reports unmeasurable, never fresh and never stale. This feed reports when RETRIEVAL last succeeded, not that any price shipped; the parsers are stubbed today (see gate), so the store stays empty and this feed reads unmeasurable until a real parser lands.
datasets.gate: none to run; first-party parsers are STUBBED (fetchFromSource returns []), so the sweep never stamps until a real per-source parser lands. Publishing retrieved rows to the served price_updates artifact still requires the human-reviewed script path.

datasets.label: Per-drink price updates
datasets.cadence: weekly, Monday 07:30 UTC
datasets.gate: none to run; only allowlisted first-party source (Wetherspoons) has no per-drink web prices, so the pipeline is real but emits zero rows

datasets.label: Food-menu price updates
datasets.cadence: episodic — harvested by hand (no workflow)
datasets.gate: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY for menu scraping harvest

datasets.label: Night signals (offline-reviewed claims)
datasets.cadence: human-gated approved publish; no machine schedule
datasets.refreshWorkflow: manual approved publish via npm run refresh:night-signals -- --open-pr; Vercel candidate ingestion never publishes reviewed claims
datasets.gate: Every claim passes human review before it ships, so this snapshot advances only on an approved publish. EXA_API_KEY arms the separate Vercel candidate-ingestion feed; it does not create a machine cadence for reviewed night_signals.

datasets.label: Night Signal candidate ingestion (Exa sweep, pending review)
datasets.cadence: daily, 05:15 UTC via Vercel cron
datasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-night-signals sweeps Exa for dated, attributable London pub buzz and stamps feed_freshness (durable store, migration 0047 plane). Store-only, no committed artifact: /api/freshness and the freshness-audit cron both read the store's real observedAt directly (never a disk fallback, because none exists), and scripts/check_freshness.mjs queries the same table dependency-free. A store the checker cannot reach reports unmeasurable, never fresh and never stale. Hard staleness-budgeting an artifact-less cron feed is a registry-model follow-up. This feed reports when INGESTION last ran, not that any claim shipped.
datasets.gate: EXA_API_KEY (present in Vercel Preview + Production). Keyless = safe no-op. Candidates stay PENDING; durable candidate persistence and a store-based review surface remain follow-up work. Reviewed night_signals still advances only through an approved human publish.

datasets.label: Night-area weather cache
datasets.cadence: every 6h via Vercel cron (0 */6 * * * UTC); observedAt is store-backed when migration 0047 is applied, else the committed file
datasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-weather → durable weather_snapshots store (read store-first via lib/weatherSnapshots.server); committed file is the pre-migration/degraded fallback. GitHub Actions retired.
datasets.gate: none (Open-Meteo is keyless — the weather feed always runs)

datasets.label: What's-On (sport / quiz / deals / music / events)
datasets.cadence: SLIM tonight-window revalidation daily via Vercel cron (0 14 * * * UTC = 15:00 London BST / 14:00 GMT); observedAt is store-backed (feed_freshness) after migration 0047, else the committed baseline file. Full ingest is out-of-function (see docs/CRON_PLANE_RUNBOOK.md).
datasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-whats-on revalidates the servable tonight window (baseline blended with live CityMCP at request time) and stamps feed_freshness. FULL ingest (baseline scrape aggregation via scripts/refresh_whats_on.mjs; events via scripts/whatson/eventsRefresh.mjs) stays a LOCAL/manual job — it needs pre-scraped agent outputs and writes committed files a read-only serverless FS cannot persist. GitHub Actions retired.
datasets.gate: Full-ingest keys: EXA_API_KEY / FIRECRAWL_API_KEY (baseline scrape), TICKETMASTER_API_KEY and/or SKIDDLE_API_KEY (events; Skiddle needs written commercial approval). Absent keys degrade loud-but-soft: the slim cron logs + skips full ingest. Baseline rows are hand-verified transforms; live layer also blends CityMCP at request time.

datasets.label: What's-On sport fixtures (derived screenings)
datasets.cadence: episodic; hand-curated fixture seed, re-derived on each manual refresh (crons dead, #408)
datasets.refreshWorkflow: manual (node scripts/whatson/sportFixtures.mjs; refresh the SPORT_FIXTURES seed from the FIFA / Premier League public schedules, then regenerate)
datasets.gate: none (bundled static; keyless). Past-dated rows are never served: lib/whatsOn.ts filterNotPast guards the serving seam in lib/whatsOnStore.ts, so a stale seed degrades to zero served fixtures rather than surfacing a played match.

datasets.label: Eventbrite own-org events (live, Tonight surface)
datasets.cadence: live — fetched per request from eventbriteapi.com, cached in-process (5 min TTL per instance, never disk-cached)
datasets.gate: EVENTBRITE_API_TOKEN. Capability-limited: Eventbrite removed public event search in 2019, so a private token can only surface the authenticated account's OWN organizations' events. Contributes 0 rows until the owner creates events under that account; lights up with no code change.

datasets.label: TfL last-train / last-drink (live)
datasets.cadence: live — fetched per request from api.tfl.gov.uk, never disk-cached
datasets.gate: none (keyless); TFL_APP_KEY only raises rate limits

datasets.label: TfL nearby bus departures (live)
datasets.cadence: live: nearby stops and per-stop arrivals fetched per request from api.tfl.gov.uk through the shared lib/tflClient.server.ts client, never disk-cached. Bounded fan-out: bus stops inside a 500 m straight-line radius, capped at 4, each asked concurrently inside one 15 s route budget. A prediction older than 2 minutes, undated, already due, or over an hour away is dropped, and an unreachable, malformed, empty or stale-only read answers unavailable rather than reporting that no bus is coming.
datasets.gate: none (keyless); TFL_APP_KEY only raises rate limits

datasets.label: TfL material disruption (night-shaping layer)
datasets.cadence: live — TfL Line Status fetched server-side and revalidated every 5 min (Next data cache), then filtered to material disruptions (suspensions, severe delays, planned closures overlapping tonight 17:00-02:00 London) touching the active night patch. No disk artifact; nothing renders when clear.
datasets.refreshWorkflow: live-per-request with 5-min server revalidate (app/api/tfl-disruption via lib/tflDisruption)
datasets.gate: none (keyless); TFL_APP_KEY only raises rate limits

datasets.label: FSA food hygiene ratings (FHRS)
datasets.cadence: live — fetched per request from api.ratings.food.gov.uk, cached in-process (24h TTL per instance, never disk-cached)
datasets.gate: none (keyless open API; requires the x-api-version: 2 header)

datasets.label: CityMCP London (buzz / status / journey / places)
datasets.cadence: live — proxied per request with short in-process TTLs (3–10 min)
datasets.gate: none (keyless upstream); buzz digest quality depends on CityMCP's own EXA-backed enrichment

datasets.label: Night calm context (data.police.uk street-level crime)
datasets.cadence: live — fetched per request from data.police.uk, aggregated to a coarse Night Area and cached per area per published month (~12h in-process TTL). Upstream publishes ~2 months in arrears; the latest available month is read from crime-last-updated.
datasets.gate: none (keyless open data). Surfaces one calm band only, never crime counts or per-street detail.

datasets.label: Historic pubs index (heritage cache × venue dataset JOIN)

datasets.gate: none (deterministic JOIN of committed heritage_cache.json + pint_prices_app_dataset.json)

stamp.consumedBy: committed snapshot; bundled into the app via lib/personaDrinks.ts (webpack inlines the JSON). This literal is the crawl's collection date, the single source of truth for how fresh the persona set is.

datasets.cadence: episodic snapshot — re-run the persona crawl (Exa + Firecrawl), drop the new JSONL in as data/persona_drinks.source.jsonl, then node scripts/build_persona_drinks.mjs
datasets.gate: none to check (bundled static). A refresh crawl needs EXA_API_KEY and FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.
